issue.description: CAND-00011 (Shelf Space Usage Report) omits an explicit requirement present in the source: branch managers must be able to see their local situation AND see how they compare to the system average. Source literal quote: "This way branch managers can see their local situation AND see how they compare to the system average." The existing candidate requires per-library and per-system reports and side-by-side comparisons across libraries, but it does not explicitly require a system-average comparison metric or presentation that makes the system-average visible alongside a branch's results.
issue.suggested_fix: Amend CAND-00011 to explicitly require the shelf-space report to present a system-average comparative value (for example: a system-average column/row, an overlay, or an explicit 'compare to system average' view) so branch managers can directly compare local percentages to the system-wide average. Document how the system average is calculated (scope, inclusion rules) and how it is displayed in side-by-side or comparison views.

reason: Source explicitly asked that branch views be comparable to a system average; CAND-00011 does not require a system-average comparative value and must be augmented.

issue.description: The existing candidate CAND-00038 (Batch Status Conversion) records the need for a batch status-conversion report/utility but omits operational and safety details that the source explicitly and repeatedly raised for batch operations. The email thread requested bulk status changes (example: changing 100 items at once) while several respondents warned about safety (avoid accidental mass changes) and asked for the same protections required for destructive purging workflows.
issue.suggested_fix: Augment CAND-00038 to include the safety and operational controls expected for bulk operations: require a preview step with a concise human-readable summary (number of items, source status(es), target status, scope), an explicit confirmation action before applying changes, an auditable log entry for every applied batch-status change (operator id, timestamp, affected item ids, source and target statuses, optional reason), and an undo/rollback capability or a documented configurable undo window and known limitations. For large selections require chunked processing with progress reporting and retry/resume semantics, and require role-based permission controls and a separate confirmation/authorization step for bulk status changes that could affect large percentages of a branch/system collection.

reason: Batch-status conversion candidates lack the safety/operational controls (preview, confirmation, auditable log, undo/rollback, chunked processing) that the sources demand for large/bulk operations; this is a substantive omission to fix.

issue.description: The candidate CAND-00039 ('Last Copy Report') is present but its captured wording focuses on the 'library system's last copies' and does not preserve the source's explicit request for both per-library (branch) and per-system views. Thomas and others explicitly asked for both scoped views and Robert described the detection rule ('for each item record, is this the only copy in the specified scope? If yes, flag it').
issue.suggested_fix: Update CAND-00039 to explicitly require both scope options (per-library/branch and per-system) and to document the precise detection logic: for each item record, evaluate whether any other copies exist within the selected scope (branch or system); if none exist, flag the item as a last copy. Also require that the report expose bibliographic identifiers and exportable context to support catalogers (as the draft's Item-purging requirement notes), and document how scope selection affects flags and any caching/replication semantics that might delay last-copy detection.

reason: The 'last copy' need in the sources requests both branch- and system-scoped views and explicit detection logic; CAND-00039 should be extended to capture both scopes and the detection rule.

issue.description: The consolidated requirement 'Patron characteristics and demographic queries' in the draft adds an obligation that "Data used to generate demographic statistics shall be anonymized prior to export or reporting; personally identifying information must be removed or aggregated...". issue.description: The Batch item transfer utility requirement in the draft lists DOC-019 as one of its sources, but the supplied source document (DOC-019 meeting notes) contains no discussion of batch item-transfer utilities, transfer-preview/undo mechanics, scheduling/revert semantics, transfer logging, chunked processing, selection UX (multi-select, select-all, persistent selection), barcode/TCN uploads, or the other detailed behaviors attributed to that requirement. Attributing these detailed batch-transfer requirements to DOC-019 is therefore false provenance.
issue.suggested_fix: Remove DOC-019 from the provenance for the batch-item-transfer-related candidate IDs unless supporting text can be added to DOC-019; alternatively, add a precise citation to the actual source document(s) that substantiate each batch-transfer sub-requirement.

reason: DOC-019 does not discuss batch item‑transfer UX/details; attributing the transfer‑utility subrequirements to DOC-019 is false provenance and the spec should correct provenance statements for those items.

issue.description: The 'Missing, damaged and in-transit reporting' requirement in the draft includes an explicit default threshold suggestion of 7 days for identifying items 'in-transit more than X days'. The DOC-019 meeting notes record only that "items that have been in-transit more than X days (X configurable)" and discuss configurable thresholds generically — they do not establish a 7-day default. The draft therefore introduces an ungrounded numeric default not present in this source.
issue.suggested_fix: Remove or re-label the 7-day 'default suggested' value from the candidate provenance to reflect that DOC-019 does not set a default; if a default is required, cite a source that specifies 7 days or document that the default was chosen by another stakeholder/process.

reason: This repeats earlier items about a 7‑day default and the corpus does include 7‑day suggestions in some places; the blanket claim that the default was introduced without any supporting source is not supported.
